title: Adaptive response TTL and staleness model — notes
content:
Context / problem statement:
- We're seeing variable freshness requirements for generated responses across products (assistant messages, personalized summaries, cached reranks). A single static TTL for cached generation results is causing either stale outward-facing UX (too long) or wasted compute (too short).
- Need an adaptive TTL/staleness model that the runtime and edge proxies can use to:
  * decide when to serve cached generations vs re-run models,
  * control stale-while-revalidate behavior, and
  * surface staleness metadata to clients for graceful UI behavior.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Minimize user-facing stale outputs while keeping token spend bounded.
- Provide predictable latency SLO impacts when cache-hit vs re-eval.
- Make policy configurable per-route and per-customer (hosted vs dedicated).
- Provide observability: staleness distributions, revalidation rates, cost delta.

High-level approach / components:
1) Response metadata baked into cached objects:
   - cached_response = {payload, model_version, computed_score, last_eval_ts, ttl_hint, staleness_score, provenance_tags}
   - ttl_hint: initial suggestion from generator (e.g., short for ephemeral prompts)
   - staleness_score: float 0..1 indicating expected semantic drift risk over time (higher -> re-eval sooner)

2) Adaptive TTL function inside runtime/edge (sketch):
   TTL_effective = clamp( base_ttl * (1 - staleness_score) * freshness_factor(model_version_age) * route_policy_multiplier, min_ttl, max_ttl )
   - base_ttl: route-level config (default 60s for chat messages, 3600s for embeddings; examples)
   - staleness_score: computed at creation by a small classifier/regressor or heuristic
   - freshness_factor(model_version_age): decays as model_version becomes older relative to a pinned/latest mapping
   - route_policy_multiplier: e.g., enterprise customers may want conservative TTLs (0.5) or longer (2.0)

3) Stale-while-revalidate modes:
   - modes: serve-stale-and-bg-refresh | block-while-refresh | serve-stale-with-indicator
   - route config allows selecting mode + concurrency caps for background revalidation to avoid thundering herd

4) API/contract changes (minimal, backward compatible):
   - New response headers in HTTP API/edge sockets:
     X-RW-Cache: HIT|MISS|REVALIDATING
     X-RW-Staleness: <score:0-1>
     X-RW-Last-Eval: <iso-ts>
     X-RW-TTL-Effective: <seconds>
   - SDK: attach same metadata to returned object under .meta.cache and .meta.staleness

5) Config sketch (route-level fields):
   {
     "adaptive_ttl": "enabled|disabled",
     "base_ttl_seconds": "int",
     "min_ttl_seconds": "int",
     "max_ttl_seconds": "int",
     "revalidate_mode": "serve-stale-and-bg-refresh",
     "staleness_model": "v1|heuristic",
     "revalidate_backoff": "ms",
     "bg_refresh_concurrency": "int",
     "serve_stale_with_indicator": "bool"
   }

Behavioral examples / scenarios:
- Assistant short-lived context (high entropy prompts): staleness_score ~0.7, base_ttl 30s -> effective ttl ~7-12s -> often triggers re-eval on next user turn
- Reranking for search (low drift): staleness_score ~0.05, base_ttl 3600s -> effective ttl ~2700s -> cache hits reduce cost substantially
- Personalization token (sensitive): route_policy_multiplier=0.2 -> effective ttl reduced, and revalidate_mode=block-while-refresh by default

Staleness scoring ideas (build incrementally):
- Heuristics: prompt category (ephemeral vs evergreen), model length, presence of time-bound entities (dates), presence of user-specific signals (profile tokens)
- Lightweight classifier: feature vector from prompt/template + context length + model id -> trained on historical re-run deltas (semantic similarity between original and re-run)
- Proxy delta estimator: when revalidate occurs, compute embed-similarity between cached and fresh output; use as training signal

Operational protections / edge cases:
- If backend model changes or quantization profile changes (model_version mismatch), always treat as TTL=0 for that cached item or force immediate bg refresh depending on policy.
- Avoid repeated bg-refresh spikes: use token-bucket per-route and jittered revalidate windows
- Cold-start: if staleness_model unknown for a route, fall back to heuristic defaults and ramp with telemetry

Observability / metrics to emit:
- cache_hit_rate_by_route, staleness_score_histogram, bg_revalidate_rate, revalidate_latency, user-facing-stale_rate (where client reported stale flag), cost_saved_tokens_by_route
- Alerts: bg_revalidate_error_rate > 1% over 5min, revalidate_thundering_detected -> raise circuit breaker

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who trains and hosts the staleness model? options: runtime team (simple pipelined job), data platform (centralized), or product-driven training sets.
- Do we expose staleness_score to customers? privacy / proprietary heuristics trade-offs.
- How to version staleness_model config safely across customer environments (hosted vs dedicated vs private)?
- UX contract: what should SDKs do when X-RW-Cache: REVALIDATING? provide callback? promise resolved with stale + fresh world?
- Should we include an explicit "confidence to serve" metric from the generator that maps to TTL_hint? (generator attach: confidence:0-1)

Mini design sketch: state machine for cached item (text diagram):
  CACHED -> (ttl_expired) -> REVALIDATING_BG -> (bg_ok) -> CACHED (updated)
                                        
  CACHED -> (ttl_expired & policy=block) -> BLOCKING_REVALIDATE -> (fresh_ready) -> CACHED
                                        
  REVALIDATING_BG -> (revalidate_fail) -> CACHED (with retry_backoff) or EVICT if repeated fails

API shape examples (JS SDK return object):
  {
    "text": "...",
    "meta": {
      "cache": "HIT",
      "staleness": "0.12",
      "last_eval": "2026-02-12T18:23:45Z",
      "ttl_effective": "1800"
    }
  }

Notes / next steps (practical):
- Prototype a heuristic staleness scorer in runtime (rules + feature flags) and bake headers; collect re-run deltas over 2 weeks for training data. (Owner: Liam)
- Add X-RW-Cache headers in edge proxy and SDKs; choose initial defaults for base_ttl by route (Owner: Priya)
- Small PR to runtime to attach ttl_hint and staleness_score at evaluation time (PR 872 is a reference for hooking metadata) (Owner: Maya)
- Instrument metrics + add Grafana dashboard: staleness score percentiles and cost delta (Owner: Jacob)

Quick prototypes / experiments to run:
- A/B experiment on chat route: control (static ttl 60s) vs adaptive-ttl (heuristic). Measure perceived stale report (client-side), token spend, and latency distribution over 2 weeks.
- Run a synthetic re-run test: sample 10k cached responses, re-run same prompt and compute embed-sim similarity. Correlate with features (prompt length, presence of dates, model id).

Notes-to-self (short):
- Keep API opt-in for tenants initially.
- Make staleness computation lightweight; avoid extra model calls during generation path if possible.
- Consider offering a small server-side "staleness prediction" microservice that batched-scoring requests for new cached items.

-- end --
